newsitem.title: UK: BUPA expands with Goldsborough buy.
newsitem.headline: BUPA expands with Goldsborough buy.

text.p: BUPA, the British private health provider, said on Friday the acquisition of Goldsborough Healthcare Plc was part of its plans to get into a broader range of healthcare delivery and healthcare services.

It is paying 76.6 million stg in cash for the healthcare services provider in a recommended 175p per share offer that takes BUPA's UK hospitals to a total of 35 and boosts its nursing homes to 76 from 44.

"This deal is entirely within our development strategy which is to get into a broader range of healthcare delivery and healthcare services for our customers," Peter Jacobs, chief executive of BUPA told Reuters in an interview.
The purchase follows on the heels of BUPA's 34 million stg acquisition of 14 nursing homes from health care company Community Hospitals Group Plc in May.
This latest offer represents a premium of 40 percent to Goldsborough's share price at the close of business on June 5, 1997.
By 0935 GMT, shares in Goldsborough, which defended itself from a hostile bid from Westminster Health Care Plc last year, had climbed 44p to stand at 170p per share.
BUPA said that 1997 has been a good year so far, "we have gained a number of significant customers this year, we are on plan and on budget," said Jacobs.
The group made a surplus before tax of 88.9 million stg in 1996 and had a capital and reserves total of 638.8 million stg.
